title: Spatial transcriptomics (Visium)
conclusion: Singlet's image-free tissue call beats a count threshold on both slides, but its spot counts trail STARsolo slightly (shared GEX counting; mouse mito genes in the chr1 NUMT are lost). visium_ffpe_human_breast: UMIs per spot rho 0.9995 vs 0.9996, profiles r 0.9687 vs 0.973 (STARsolo), tissue kappa 0.8398 vs 0.8267 (Otsu); visium_mouse_brain_ant: UMIs per spot rho 0.9948 vs 0.9982, profiles r 0.9656 vs 0.9888 (STARsolo), tissue kappa 0.8498 vs 0.7757 (Otsu).
methods:
**Data.** 10x Visium mouse brain, sagittal anterior section 1 (CC BY 4.0), processed from its published FASTQs with 10x
GRCm39-2024-A. Truth: the Space Ranger 1.1.0 published spot matrix (exonic counts) and tissue positions. Space Ranger
detects tissue from the H&E image.

**Singlet 1.0.0.** `singlet encode --protocol 10x-visium`, then the standard pipeline. Spot barcodes are matched to the
visium-v1 spot list (4,992 spots, rebuilt from three 10x public datasets; exact or unique Hamming-1). Tissue is detected
from counts alone, without the image:
- a two-component mixture on log10 UMIs per spot;
- mean-field smoothing on the hexagonal array, with per-spot evidence capped so that six concordant neighbours decide.

Tissue spots are the sample's called set. Exon counts (spliced + ambiguous molecules) are compared, because Space Ranger
1.1 counts exonic reads only.

**Competitors.**
- Counts: STARsolo 2.7.11b with the same spot list, Cell Ranger-like settings (CB 1 mismatch with pseudocounts, UMI
  1MM_CR, MultiGeneUMI_CR, CellRanger4 adapter clipping), same FASTQs, reference and threads.
- Tissue: an Otsu threshold on log10 UMIs per spot, the usual count-based fallback when no image is available.

**Metrics.** Genes are matched by Ensembl id. The first three metrics are over Space Ranger's tissue spots:
- Spearman of UMIs per spot and of genes per spot with Space Ranger;
- median per-spot Pearson of log-CPM expression profiles with Space Ranger;
- Spearman of molecules per gene summed over the tissue spots;
- Cohen's kappa of the tissue call with Space Ranger over all 4,992 spots.

All are match-or-beat against the competitor, with no tolerance.

caveats: Binary: this branch (ATAC/Visium code) merged onto prod/modality-fixes, not yet part of the singlet-campaign build the other capabilities use; the results describe the code that the merge will bring.

Barcode lists (scATAC whitelist, ARC ATAC-GEX pairs, visium-v1 spots) were rebuilt from 10x public datasets (CC BY 4.0); the 737K-cratac-v1.txt bundled before this change is a copy of the 3' v2 list and matches ~1% of scATAC barcodes.

Spot counts use Singlet's general GEX counting. On GRCm39 it drops multimapping reads that overlap only one gene, so mt-Co2, mt-Atp6, mt-Co3 and mt-Nd3 (covered by the chr1 NUMT) are nearly absent (mt-Co3: 71 vs Space Ranger 1.7 M); STARsolo and Space Ranger keep them. This, not the Visium handling, drives the mouse count failures and affects every mouse sample; reported for the gex-counts owner.
Tissue detection uses counts only; Space Ranger's call comes from the H&E image. Model constants were fixed on synthetic data before any Visium run.
FFPE probe reads are antisense: STARsolo was run with --soloStrand Reverse; Singlet detected the strand itself.
